name: es30-framebuffer-invalidate
title: Framebuffer invalidation and attachment queries
summary: glInvalidateFramebuffer and glInvalidateSubFramebuffer on a framebuffer object (color textures and renderbuffer, packed depth/stencil, regions, READ/DRAW/FRAMEBUFFER targets, texture layers and cube faces) and on the default framebuffer: legal calls raise no error, the errors ES 3.0 section 4.5 defines are raised and change nothing, every attachment and region that was not invalidated keeps its contents bit for bit, and rendering afterwards works. Plus the attachment queries the other framebuffer demos skip: TEXTURE_LAYER, TEXTURE_LEVEL, TEXTURE_CUBE_MAP_FACE, COMPONENT_TYPE of float / signed / unsigned / normalized formats and the DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT rules.
spec: ES 3.0 §4.5 Invalidating Framebuffer Contents (glInvalidateFramebuffer, glInvalidateSubFramebuffer, every listed error; contents become undefined, nothing else is touched)

ES 3.0 §6.1.13 Framebuffer Object Queries (OBJECT_TYPE/NAME, TEXTURE_LEVEL, TEXTURE_CUBE_MAP_FACE, TEXTURE_LAYER, COMPONENT_TYPE, component sizes, DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT rules, attachment argument errors)

ES 3.0 §4.4.2.3 Attaching Renderbuffer Images, §4.4.2.4 Attaching Texture Images (glFramebufferTexture2D, glFramebufferTextureLayer and their errors), Table 4.6 Framebuffer attachment points, Table 6.14 attachment point state
ES 3.0 §4.4.4 Framebuffer Completeness, §3.8.3 Texture Image Specification (Tables 3.13 and 3.14: renderable formats and component types), §3.8.4 Immutable-Format Texture Images
ES 3.0 §4.3.3 Copying Pixels (glBlitFramebuffer, used only to show the images), §4.1.4 Stencil Test, §4.1.5 Depth Buffer Test, §4.2.3 Clearing the Buffers
ES 3.0 §2.1.6.2 Conversion from Floating-Point to Normalized Fixed-Point (equation 2.3), §2.5 GL Errors
ES 3.2 §9.2.8 (glFramebufferTextureLayer with a cube map), §9.2.3 Framebuffer Object Queries
GLSL ES 3.00 §4.3.8.2 Output Layout Qualifiers, §7.1 gl_VertexID, §7.2 gl_FragCoord

api.glInvalidateFramebuffer: COLOR_ATTACHMENT0..2, DEPTH, STENCIL, DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT of a framebuffer object, on the READ / DRAW / FRAMEBUFFER targets, on a texture layer / 3D slice / cube face and on the default framebuffer (COLOR, DEPTH, STENCIL): no error, every attachment and image that was not listed is unchanged (colors read back, depth and stencil probed with tested draws; the other half of a packed image is preserved); empty list, absent attachments and an incomplete framebuffer are no-ops; INVALID_ENUM for default-framebuffer tokens on a framebuffer object and framebuffer-object attachments on the default framebuffer, INVALID_OPERATION for COLOR_ATTACHMENT(MAX_COLOR_ATTACHMENTS), INVALID_VALUE for numAttachments = -1; failed calls invalidate nothing; rendering after the invalidation reproduces the original images
api.glInvalidateSubFramebuffer: regions inside, partly outside (negative origin, beyond the image), entirely outside and of size 0 on color, depth/stencil and the default framebuffer: no error and everything outside the region is unchanged; INVALID_ENUM and INVALID_OPERATION as above, INVALID_VALUE for numAttachments, width or height = -1
api.glGetFramebufferAttachmentParameteriv: TEXTURE_LAYER of 2D array and 3D layers (0..3, mip level 1), TEXTURE_LEVEL, TEXTURE_CUBE_MAP_FACE of the six faces (0 for non-cube textures), COMPONENT_TYPE of 22 texture formats (normalized, signed normalized, float, signed and unsigned integer), of 9 renderbuffer formats and of a texture without an image (NONE), OBJECT_TYPE / OBJECT_NAME / sizes through DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT, INVALID_OPERATION for DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT COMPONENT_TYPE and for different depth and stencil objects, INVALID_ENUM for texture state of a renderbuffer attachment and for unlisted attachments, INVALID_OPERATION for pname on an empty attachment, for COLOR_ATTACHMENT(MAX_COLOR_ATTACHMENTS) and (XFAIL on Mesa, which raises INVALID_ENUM) for non-BACK/DEPTH/STENCIL on the default framebuffer
api.glFramebufferTextureLayer: array layers 0..3 and 3D slices 0..3 of level 0 and 1 attached: the rendered pattern lands in exactly that layer (all four layers read back, the others keep the clear color); INVALID_VALUE for layer -1, MAX_ARRAY_TEXTURE_LAYERS, MAX_3D_TEXTURE_SIZE and level 100, INVALID_OPERATION for a plain 2D texture; a failed call changes nothing (queried); a cube map is accepted in a 3.2 context
api.glFramebufferTexture2D: cube faces +X..-Z, 2D mip level 2, array/3D images through the work and view framebuffers, DEPTH24_STENCIL8 / DEPTH_COMPONENT32F / integer / float textures attached for the queries; INVALID_OPERATION with a 3D texture
api.glFramebufferRenderbuffer: RGBA8 renderbuffer at COLOR_ATTACHMENT2, DEPTH24_STENCIL8 at DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT, separate DEPTH_COMPONENT16 and STENCIL_INDEX8 at the two points, integer and depth renderbuffers for COMPONENT_TYPE
api.glCheckFramebufferStatus: COMPLETE for the subject, peer and probe framebuffers and for every renderable format of the COMPONENT_TYPE table
api.glGenFramebuffers: work, view, subject, peer, probe and empty framebuffers
api.glBindFramebuffer: FRAMEBUFFER, READ_FRAMEBUFFER and DRAW_FRAMEBUFFER bound separately for the target-argument tests
api.glRenderbufferStorage: RGBA8, DEPTH24_STENCIL8, DEPTH_COMPONENT16/24/32F, STENCIL_INDEX8, integer color renderbuffers
api.glTexStorage2D: cube map, 2D mip chain, 4 x 4 format-test textures
api.glTexStorage3D: 2D array and 3D textures with a three-level mip chain
api.glBlitFramebuffer: NEAREST copy of each 64x64 image stretched onto its window cell: every pixel of every cell equals the CPU pattern pixel the blit reads for it (+-1; either neighbour within 0.05 pixel of a source pixel edge)
api.glReadBuffer: selects the color attachment glReadPixels reads (C0, C1, C2)
api.glReadPixels: RGBA/UNSIGNED_BYTE readback of every compared image and of the default framebuffer
api.glClear: COLOR/DEPTH/STENCIL of the fills, of the layers (isolation test) and of the default framebuffer after its invalidation
api.glClearColor: clear colors observed in the read-back images
api.glClearDepthf: depth 1 before the scene and in the probe negative control
api.glClearStencil: stencil 0 before the scene and in the probe negative control
api.glEnable: DEPTH_TEST, STENCIL_TEST and SCISSOR_TEST for the scene, the probes and the default-framebuffer test
api.glScissor: limits the default-framebuffer clear after its invalidation to 32 x 32 pixels
api.glDepthFunc: ALWAYS to write the scene, LESS in the probes and in the default-framebuffer depth test
api.glDepthMask: FALSE in every probe pass (probes leave depth unchanged)
api.glStencilFunc: ALWAYS/REPLACE to write the scene, EQUAL k in the probes
api.glStencilOp: REPLACE writes the scene's stencil values; KEEP in every probe
api.glGetUniformLocation: u_rect, u_z, u_base, u_size, u_color located; effects visible in the images
api.glUniform3f: u_base: every image's own base color is measured in its pixels

visual_review.notes: Window-filling layout reviewed on llvmpipe captures at 640x400 and 800x800 and the 256x256 radeonsi es-max capture. The 16 cells partition the window; each 64x64 image is stretched onto its cell with a NEAREST blit (8 stripes per cell, shade dark to bright left to right): red, green, blue, yellow (cube +X -X +Y -Y), magenta, cyan, orange, violet, light green, pink, steel blue, olive, lilac, teal, then the two mrt.frag charts with their channel permutation. All cells distinct, no seams or gaps.
